b: This year has been difficult for me. I’ve had to let go of several things (and people) I wasn’t ready to let go of: a big movie project I’d worked on for three years fell apart at the finish line, a close friend betrayed me, and my brother died in his sleep.
This cascade led to business struggles, health complications, financial uncertainty, all of which required a mystifying mixture of surrender and resolve.
To boot, my daughter became a teenager this summer. Watching her grow up is a delight. But it also means saying goodbye to the idealized portrait of the little girl I once knew.
To make sense of all my newfound grief and anger and self-pity, I started writing my eighth book, tentatively titled How to Let Go.

When I shared early excerpts with loved ones, they laughed out loud at some of the saddest parts. What a pleasant surprise. I’d been sitting alone with those stories for so long that it hadn’t occurred to me there was anything funny in them.

Hearing people laugh made me wonder whether How to Let Go belonged on the stage more than on the page. So I closed my laptop and spent a hundred hours transforming the material into my first one-man show.
Don’t get me wrong. I adore books—print books, ebooks, audiobooks—but I’ve never seen a live book before. Until now. I love how this one changes a little every night, depending on who’s in the room.
Which brings me to my exciting news…
After testing the show in Seattle, Vancouver, and New York this year, I’m bringing the How to Let Go Tour to 11 more cities in 2027.
Come spend an evening with me in any of the following cities. We’ll laugh a lot, cry a little, and talk about why it’s so hard to let go when you’re not ready.
I can’t wait to see you!
Send me a direct message if you have any local restaurant recommendations.
P.S. I still have one more stop this year. I’ll be in Los Angeles on December 11. There are a few tickets left.
